page: Google Cloud Platform f1-micro is a burstable, budget-oriented virtual machine instance within the f1 family. It features a single shared vCPU based on the Intel Xeon x86_64 architecture, operating with one physical core and one thread. The instance is equipped with 0.6 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 0.6 GB per core. It does not include any local NVMe SSD storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place the f1-micro in the bottom 10% across all performance categories. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests both scored 384.79, reflecting its shared-core CPU allocation. Memory bandwidth is limited, with a read-only small block speed of 80.8 GB/sec and a write large block speed of 0.2 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput is recorded at 0.22 GB/sec. Given these constraints, the instance is highly cost-efficient for low-demand, intermittent workloads but unsuitable for resource-intensive applications. It is best utilized for lightweight tasks such as basic web serving, microservices, cron jobs, and development testing.
description: Google Cloud Platform f1-micro is a budget-tier, shared-core virtual machine designed for lightweight workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features a single shared Intel Xeon vCPU with one physical core and 0.6 GB of RAM. The instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks place the f1-micro in the bottom 10% of tested servers, with a stress-ng CPU score of 384.79 and a static web serving throughput of 0.22 GB/sec. Memory write bandwidth is also constrained at 0.2 GB/sec. This highly economical instance is best suited for low-traffic web serving, basic scripting, cron jobs, and small-scale development or testing environments where resource demands are minimal and intermittent.
